study_material.title: Simple and Compound Interest - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Simple interest grows linearly (interest only on the principal); compound interest grows geometrically (interest on interest). Placement questions revolve around the two formulas, the CI-SI difference shortcut, and doubling-time reasoning.
learning_objectives: Apply SI = PTR/100 and CI = P(1 + R/100)^T - P fluently
Use the 2-year and 3-year CI-SI difference shortcuts
Reverse-engineer principal, rate or time from given interest

concepts.heading: 1. Simple Interest
concepts.body: SI = P x T x R / 100, Amount = P + SI. Interest each year is identical (PR/100), so SI problems are linear equations in disguise. If a sum becomes n times itself in T years at SI, then R = 100(n-1)/T.

concepts.heading: 2. Compound Interest
concepts.body: Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T; CI = Amount - P. Each year's interest joins the principal for the next year. Successive-percentage logic applies: 2 years at 10% is a net 21% growth (10 + 10 + 100/100).

concepts.heading: 3. Compounding Frequency
concepts.body: For half-yearly compounding, halve the rate and double the time: Amount = P(1 + R/200)^(2T). For quarterly, quarter the rate and quadruple the time. More frequent compounding always yields slightly more interest.

concepts.heading: 4. CI - SI Difference
concepts.body: For 2 years: difference = P(R/100)^2. For 3 years: difference = P(R/100)^2 x (3 + R/100). These shortcuts crack the common 'difference between CI and SI' questions in seconds.

concepts.heading: 5. Growth Multiples
concepts.body: At SI, a sum doubling in T years means PTR/100 = P, so R = 100/T. At CI, doubling depends on (1 + R/100)^T = 2; useful anchors: 10% doubles in about 7.3 years, and if a sum becomes k times in T years at CI, it becomes k^2 times in 2T years.

shortcut_methods: Two years at r% CI = net (2r + r^2/100)% growth
At CI, k times in T years means k^2 times in 2T years
Percentage-change chain logic works for CI: multiply factors
common_mistakes: Using the SI formula for compound problems and vice versa
Forgetting to adjust rate and time for half-yearly compounding
Subtracting principal incorrectly - CI is amount minus principal
Assuming CI doubling time is 100/R years (that is SI logic)
study_material.summary: SI is linear, CI is exponential. Memorise both formulas, the frequency adjustment, and the CI-SI difference shortcuts - that covers nearly every question.

solved_examples.question: Find the simple interest on Rs. 5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
Find the compound interest on Rs. 10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years.
A sum doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. Find the rate.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Doubling means SI = P, so PTR/100 = P gives R = 100/8 = 12.5%.
solved_examples.shortcut: R x T = 100 for doubling at SI.
